source.title: Edo question formation: polar, alternative and non-polar questions
source.note: Transcribed from OCR text of a linguistics paper on Edo (Bini). Title, author, year and bibliography were not in the text.
source.language: Edo (Bini), Niger-Congo; main language of the ancient Kingdom of Benin
missing_from_text: Title, author, year, bibliography, section 1 and the start of section 2
Numbers and glosses of examples (1)-(3); section 2.1 on raised pitch
Methods 2-5 of section 3 and everything after example (17)
transcription_caveats: ä, ö and ü are OCR corruptions of tone-marked vowels, not Edo orthography. edo_as_printed keeps them; edo_reading drops them. Tone marks are not reconstructed.
edo_reading corrects Edo forms only where the gloss or another example makes the word clear (e.g. bkhub -> okhuo, ehe -> ebe, ghd -> gha).
The verb and noun negators are garbled in the prose; ma and i are inferred from examples (5), (7) and (10).

The source glosses rre as 'come' in (4), (9) and (13), and ne as 'come' in (14). Examples are recorded as printed, but the project owner confirms the Edo word for 'come' is lare, which is what academy_vocabulary uses.
A duplicate copy of the opening text was supplied and has been left out.

examples.note: Same word with question vs statement pitch; pitch marks lost.
First word of translation cut off.

examples.translation: 'Is it food that Osaro is eating?'
'It is not food that Osaro is eating either'.

examples.edo_as_printed: Ösaro bo owä ra Ösärorhie bkhub?
examples.edo_reading: Osaro bo owa ra Osaro rhie okhuo?
examples.gloss: Osaro build house or-Q Osaro take woman
examples.translation: 'Did Osaro build a house or Osaro married a woman?'
'No, he did not build a house.'
'No, he did not marry a woman.'

examples.edo_as_printed: Ovbokhän nie qnä khin ra otuen?
examples.gloss: wife your this-one be or-Q relation-your
examples.translation: 'Is this your wife or your relation?'
examples.note: Gloss-to-word alignment scrambled in the scan; qnä is probably ọna.
